note.label: Song of Solomon 5: My Beloved Is White and Ruddy

precepts.why:
“My beloved is white and ruddy”: Christianity argues these verses prove the beloved is a white man, but white in the scriptures does not mean white skin. “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

David is not asking for a change of skin. White means undefiled and unspotted, clean and clear, made clean. There is nobody who is literally white; the beloved is white in the sense David means here.

note.label: Song of Solomon 5: My Beloved Is White and Ruddy

precepts.why:
If the scriptures speak of a red man, it is not the Israelites. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.”

Esau is the red man, the very one Christianity tries to attribute the Israelites to. Ruddy does not mean red either; it means a healthy, youthful appearance with clean, clear, beautiful skin.

precepts.text: Young David was ruddy and of a beautiful countenance and goodly to look to, and the Most High said arise and anoint him, showing ruddy is a healthy youthful appearance.
precepts.point: His head is as the most fine gold, and his locks are bushy and black as a raven; this is the same as reading of the Christ having woolly hair and the Most High having hair of pure wool.

note.label: Song of Solomon 5: My Beloved Is White and Ruddy

precepts.why:
Ruddy is the same word used of young King David. “Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the Lord said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.”

Ruddy goes with a beautiful countenance and being goodly to look to: a healthy, youthful appearance with clean, clear, beautiful skin, not red. Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brethren, “and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” That is what ruddy means of the beloved.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire”. The Christ has woolly hair, like the bushy locks of the beloved described here.

And his hairs being white like wool is the same white as before: undefiled and clean, not white skin.

note.label: Song of Solomon 5: My Beloved Is White and Ruddy

precepts.why:
The beloved's locks are bushy. Judith “braided the hair of her head, and put on a tire upon it, and put on her garments of gladness, wherewith she was clad during the life of Manasses her husband.”

This is why it matters for the sisters to return to their natural bushy hair and stop putting chemicals in it, laying down the fashions of the world. Judith washed, anointed herself with precious ointment and braided her own hair.
